intro: A single temporal-difference residual uses a nearby prediction. Generalized advantage estimation blends residuals farther into the rollout while respecting episode boundaries.
task: Return GAE advantages and corresponding value targets. Compare trace decay zero and one to see how much future evidence enters each estimate.
requirements: rewards and terminated have length T in 1..255. values has length T+1 and includes the prediction after the final transition. terminated is numeric zero/one; discount and trace_decay are scalars in [0,1].

Return {"advantages": A, "targets": lambda_returns}. In exact arithmetic, lambda_returns=A+values[:-1]. Compute targets with the equivalent recurrence L[T]=values[T], L[t]=rewards[t]+discount*(1-terminated[t])*((1-trace_decay)*values[t+1]+trace_decay*L[t+1]) to preserve small terminal rewards beside large values. Do not normalize advantages or train a value network.

Use real finite numeric inputs of magnitude at most 1e30, excluding boolean parameters. Vectors have 1..256 entries and each matrix axis has length 1..256 unless a stricter bound is stated. Leave caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Compute residuals first
hints.body: The last supplied value is a bootstrap prediction, not another reward.

hints.title: Mask both future terms
hints.body: A terminal flag stops both the value bootstrap in delta and the advantage trace.

explanation: At trace decay zero, the estimate is the one-step residual. At trace decay one, adding the current value back telescopes the residual sequence into a bootstrapped return.
Intermediate trace decay values reduce the influence of distant residuals. This is an estimator from a fixed rollout, not a guarantee of improved policy learning.
